liz: Heads-up — prototype for a 'request-morpher' to bridge v3 clients to v4 runtime is live on staging. Want a quick design + rollout sync.

anna: saw it. quick q — does it mutate body or rely on headers?

liz: body morphing for legacy clients: wrap the old payload in an envelope, add header `X-RI-Compat: v3`. minimal gateway changes. example: ```{
  "legacy": { ...original body... },
  "meta": { "morphed_from": "v3" }
}```

tariq: tradeoffs: body wrapping avoids gateway rule churn but adds CPU/parse overhead and breaks streaming semantics for some endpoints. also harder for size-limited requests.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary started in us-west-2 -> svc/req-morpher @ 10% traffic.

ben: telemetry note — we must emit granular metrics: `morph.request.count`, `morph.latency.p50/p95`, `morph.schema_miss.count`. tag with `compat=legacy-v3` and tenant id. Also capture a sample of transformed payloads for debugging (scrub PII).

anna: can we make morpher idempotent for retries? idea: detect envelope and noop; set header `X-RI-Morphed: 1` so downstream knows it was transformed. this avoids double-wrapping.

liz: agreed. also need a circuit-breaker path: on heavy errors morpher should short-circuit and return 412 with `X-RI-Compat-Failed: <reason>` so clients get deterministic failure instead of timeouts. we'll surface that in Console as a per-route alert.

tariq: about deprecation policy — how long do we expect to run this morpher? we should give customers a timeline and an opt-in flag per tenant. propose: default enabled for 12 months, `compat-mode` flag to keep on longer, then deprecate.

liz: :thumbsup: plan: run canary for 48h, collect metrics (latency + error delta + morph-rate), then expand to 10% global for 7 days. I'll open a follow-up RFC that includes: rollout stages, runtime knobs (`enable`, `max_payload_bytes`, `sample_rate`), telemetry schema, and sample HTTP examples. will ping accounts with >0.1% morph-rate.

ben: also add a toggle in Redwood Console to view per-tenant morph metrics and to flip `compat-mode`. ops should be able to opt-out quickly if we see regressions.

opsbot: opsbot: Note — created alert: `morph_error_rate > 1%` -> pager for eng-runtime on-call.

anna: cool. I'll review the RFC draft and iterate on the error semantics. small suggestion: prefer 422 over 412 for payload transformation errors? 422 might map better to unprocessable entity.

liz: good call. we'll evaluate both and pick the most semantically clear code in RFC. thanks all — follow-up RFC link will land in this thread.
